newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK BLUE CHIPS MIXED, SAX INDEX DIPS 0.4 PTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK BLUE CHIPS MIXED, SAX INDEX DIPS 0.4 PTS.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed
in listless trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on
Wednesday, and the SAX index dipped 0.4 points to 201.7.
Brokers said the current bearish mood was expected to
extend through the end of this year.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta lost 10 crowns to close
at 1,960, and brokers said some foreign investors were
apparently selling their holdings in the company.
Refiner Slovnaft closed one crown lower at 939.
"Slovnaft has been showing a clear downward trend, which
should continue in the near future, but it's hard to predict
where the fall may stop," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
VUB bank closed unchanged at 1,650 crowns, as the situation
in the bank remained unclear ahead of expected banking sector
privatisations.
VUB's shares held by the Czech state National Property Fund
makes the privatisation more dificult than in fully Slovak
state-controled banks.
Steel producer VSZ was the only top stock to post a gain,
closing up 15 crowns at 630.
Overall volume fell to 77,226 shares, from 707,793 shares
on Tuesday, and turnover decreased to 38.39 million crowns,
from 166.85 million.
-- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
